newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Albright finds fault with Czech interpreter.
newsitem.headline: Albright finds fault with Czech interpreter.

text.p: Czech-born U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright harried her Czech language interpreter on Monday, correcting him three times at a news conference with Czech President Vaclav Havel.
The State Department interpreter, Ivo Reznick, finally gave up and allowed his counterpart for Havel take over translating Albright's remarks as well.

Despite having lived most of her life in the United States, Albright still speaks Czech fluently and used no interpreter in her talks with Havel during a visit to her birthplace Prague as part of a central and east European tour.

Faced with the unenviable task of translating Albright's English into her native tongue at the subsequent news conference, Reznick ran into trouble with a phrase in her opening remarks praising Havel for staying true to his life-long ideals.
"Not exactly," she commented acidly on the interpreter's effort. She repeated her remark, and when Reznick hesitated, improvised her own translation to laughter from journalists.
Reznick had more problems soon afterwards with the expression "rogue states". He stumbled through a lengthy paraphrase, prompting Albright to intervene again.
The increasingly nervous interpreter was berated yet again by Albright over his translation of a question in English about a meeting she held last week with Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar.
After Albright had replied in English, Reznick asked the journalist to repeat the second half of his double-headed question, leading Albright to interrupt sharply: "Translate my answer."
At this point, Havel's interpreter stepped in.

Albright, who speaks at least four languages, has skirmished with interpreters before. During an interview in St Petersburg with Russian television on Sunday she told a translator he had missed out part of her remarks.
